title: Can Bangladesh turn US fibre purchases into tariff advantage?
content:
Bangladesh’s US trade deal set a 19 per cent tariff and tied zero-tariff apparel access to US cotton and man-made-fibre purchases.
A July Section 301 action added a 10 per cent duty and directed three-year textile TRQs for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia.
Quota size, allocation and timing remain pending; gains depend on US fibre costs, legal stability and exporter access.

title: South India cotton yarn faces sluggish demand; prices stable
content:
South India cotton yarn trade remains sluggish as weak fabric lifting keeps buyers cautious; Mumbai and Tiruppur prices stay steady.
Spinning mills seek higher yarn rates to offset rising fibre costs, with Indian cotton yarn becoming more attractive in export markets.
Gujarat cotton is range-bound as buyers await delayed new-crop arrivals, while firmer cottonseed prices support the market.

title: US cotton exports sharply dip but Upland shipments on rise
content:
US Upland cotton net sales for 2026-27 fell about 71 per cent week on week to 27,500 RB, with India and Vietnam the largest buyers at 10,800 RB each.
Upland shipments rose about 4.7 per cent to 189,500 RB, led by Vietnam, India, Pakistan, Mexico and Indonesia.
Pima sales dropped about 14 per cent to 1,800 RB, while shipments fell about 47 per cent to 4,600 RB.

title: ICE cotton climbs on stronger crude oil, hopes of Chinese buying
content:
ICE cotton futures rose for a second day, with December 2026 settling at 88.22 cents as crude oil jumped around 4 per cent.
US heat and adverse weather kept crop-loss concerns alive, while ratings fell to 34 per cent Good/Excellent before Friday’s WASDE report.
Possible Chinese import demand supported sentiment, but a stronger US dollar and weaker ZCE cotton limited confirmation.

title: Bangladesh apparel exports price to US drops 2.26% YoY in Jan-Jul 2026
content:
The average price of Bangladesh’s apparel exports to the US fell by 2.26 per cent YoY in the first seven months this year. 
There was also a 6.5-per cent drop in Bangladesh's apparel export value to the US during the period, while shipment volume dropped by 4.34 per cent YoY. 
Not all exporters bore the additional tariff burden equally; in some cases, buyers and exporters shared the cost.

title: Inditex navigates war, tariffs and still delivers
content:
Middle East disruptions lifted Inditex’s transport and input costs in the first half, affecting gross margin and operating expenditure in the second quarter.
The Zara owner has 480 franchise stores in the Middle East, all open, but geopolitical conditions are impacting regional sales.
First-half gross margin rose 40 basis points to 58.7 per cent, while net income increased 6.8 per cent to €3.

title: India’s US apparel exports fall 26%; Bangladesh overtakes China
content:
In January–July 2026, US apparel imports from India fell about 26 per cent to $2.45 billion, Office of Textiles and Apparel data show.
Total US apparel imports declined roughly 9 per cent to about $41.8 billion.
Vietnam led at about $9.37 billion, while Bangladesh reached $4.66 billion and moved ahead of China.
Cambodia and Indonesia increased shipments as China fell by about one-third.

title: Argentina apparel imports rise 31.7% in Jan-Jul after liberalisation
content:
Argentina’s apparel imports reached $468.262 million in January-July 2026, up 31.73 per cent year on year. 
China held a 52.03 per cent share, while Vietnam and Bangladesh grew 50.62 per cent and 54.52 per cent, respectively. 
Imports nearly doubled in 2025 as liberalised trade, easier payment access and price-competitive Asian hubs supported apparel sourcing.

title: US' Caleres lifts FY26 EPS outlook as Q2 sales rise 5.6%
content:
Caleres expects low-to-mid-single-digit fiscal 2026 sales growth and lifted the lower end of adjusted EPS guidance to $1.50.
Second-quarter net sales rose 5.6 per cent to $695.5 million and GAAP net earnings reached $58.6 million, aided by tariff refunds.
Brand Portfolio sales grew 23.6 per cent, offsetting lower Famous Footwear sales amid a delayed Back-to-School season.
